children: The tenure of Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been marked by a fundamental transformation in the way India approaches and leverages technology. On the occasion of the Prime Minister’s birthday, it is an opportune moment to reflect on what the country has achieved in terms of digital reach and infrastructure, and to consider what the next phase of India’s technology journey could hold.

The introduction of Digital India in 2015 was a major milestone in this journey because that was when technology became more central to the development agenda focused on digitally delivering services and achieving connectivity. Eleven years on, the foundations laid at that time have expanded into the current digital ecosystem.

UPI is perhaps the best example of the evolution of the ecosystem. Once, it was just a new payments application launched in 2016; now, it has become a thick foundation of India’s payment infrastructure with UPI recording more than 24,000 crore transactions in 2025-26.

This change has also brought about a change in the way businesses view technology as far as enterprise is concerned. The discussion has surpassed mere digitization to reach data, analytics, cloud and artificial intelligence. Firms are now more inclined towards using technology to not just automate their tasks but also improve decision-making and create new opportunities.

This is quite important because this marks the beginning of a new phase in the technology journey of India. The digital foundation put in place during the last decade needs to be turned into a productivity booster, and to support innovation and value generation. This will need ongoing investments in AI, data infrastructure, cybersecurity, cloud resources and, just as importantly, professionals.

When observing PM Modi’s journey through the prism of technology, we can see how this cabinet has transformed digital infrastructure from merely an auxiliary component of economic policymaking to a significant strategic ingredient in India’s development agenda. The new challenge is to take this further step and ensure India turns into not just a huge technology market, but also into a significant technology creator with multiple intellectual property rights and globally applicable digital solutions.
In my opinion, this is an opportunity to transform the capabilities India managed to develop over the last decade into the country’s sustained innovation and profitability.
Chanakya Bellam Radhakrishna, Whole Time Director,
